test_policy.notes: Page says SAT and ACT scores do not influence the admission decision and are not required; scores may be submitted but are not used.

requirements.notes: Common Application or the University of Maine System application. The $50 application fee applies to international applicants only (free for US and Canadian applicants). International first-year applicants submit official secondary transcripts with certified English translations, financial documentation, and a school counselor statement and/or recommendation letter; a personal essay is recommended. Admission is based primarily on academic background, course rigor and grades. BS in Nursing first-year applications are due Feb 1 and nursing is admitted for fall only.

deadlines.label: Early action application deadline
deadlines.notes: Supporting materials due Dec 15; admission decision guaranteed by Jan 15 if both are met. Dates print no year, so the fall 2027 entry cycle is assumed.

deadlines.label: Priority deadline for academic scholarship consideration
deadlines.notes: Supporting materials due Feb 15. The international scholarship page says international applicants who apply by the stated deadline are automatically considered; the stated international deadline is June 1.

deadlines.label: International student application deadline - fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: USM admits on a rolling basis. Both the international programs page and the undergraduate admission page list June 1 for international fall applicants (the general final fall deadline is Aug 15). Spring entry deadline for international students is Oct 15. No year is printed, so fall 2027 is assumed.

english_policy.waiver_notes: The English language requirements page lists minimum test scores only and states no waiver rules; confirm exemptions with the Office of Admissions. An Admissions Pathway Program (undergraduate only) accepts lower scores: TOEFL 60, IELTS 5.5-6.0, PTE 46, Duolingo 90. An Intensive ESOL program accepts TOEFL 45, IELTS 5.0, Duolingo 75.

english.notes: Direct entry to undergraduate degree programs; internet-based and superscored. Pathway program minimum 60.

cost.notes: International undergraduate budget for 2026-27 (Tuition Level 1; Level 2 $30,870 and Level 3 $32,580 depending on major; totals $53,490 / $55,260 / $56,970): tuition $29,100, academic fees $3,390, room and board $14,000, books $1,000, health insurance $3,000 and personal expenses $3,000 (shown together as other). In-state and out-of-state 2026-27 tuition were not found; College Navigator 2024-25 lists tuition and fees of $11,284 in-state and $27,944 out-of-state

aid.notes: All international undergraduates who apply by the deadline are automatically considered for merit scholarships, awarded at admission by high school GPA and renewable for 4 years: USM Scholar (GPA 2.75-2.99) $7,000/year, Dirigo Scholar (3.0-3.49) $11,000/year, Presidential Scholar (3.5+) $11,000/year, plus a one-time $2,000 Presidential Recognition Award (3.5+). A $1,000/year housing scholarship is available to those who indicated interest in on-campus housing. The page lists only merit awards and no need-based aid for international students, so need-based aid is left unconfirmed. An Admissions Pathway Program and Intensive ESOL program are available for students below the direct-entry English scores.

sat.note: CEEB code printed on the undergraduate admission page; scores are optional and not used in decisions.

act.note: No ACT code printed on the admission page; look it up at act.org.
